utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now in the course of your review and analysis for this case and this report for the Mladic case, did you have occasion to review any information about the training and qualifications of the ABiH operators who were said to be engaged in radio surveillance work?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A specific document? Well, on the basis of everything, I managed to conclude that these units received personnel from the former JNA, but very few such people, then from the Ministry of the Interior, and ham radio operators. These were three categories of people, as far as I could conclude, in units for EiPED in the units of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's not responsive.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution object to an answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Review any information? What information is he basing this on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, he is telling us that there were no specific documents. But, Mr. Ivetic, if you -- one second, please. Well, he gave his sources. That's everything. Based on everything, the witness managed to conclude. If that is the information the witness had, then the probative value of that answer is limited, Mr. Ivetic. So if you want better evidence, please further explore. Mr. McCloskey, this, to some extent, I would say, meets your concerns?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Absolutely, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, being careful not to mention any names, did you have occasion to review any witness statements of the ABiH operators?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, while reading a statement of an, I mean, official --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me intervene. First of all, Mr. Ivetic, I think it's not for you to tell the witness not to mention any names, unless you had specific names on your mind. You put a question to the witness. And if you have any concerns about protection, then you could suggest to go into private session, and then the witness can fully answer the question. That, I think, is the appropriate way of proceeding. Perhaps then we should go --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- do that rather than to tell the witness not give any names.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session for a moment so that you can freely answer the question, including any names you may be aware of.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could look at page 42 in the Serbian and page 29 in the English of your report and look at 10.3 of the same. In the first part of 10.3, you say that the ABH monitoring -- you talk about the ABH monitoring of radio communications. Does this mean they could monitor and understand secure radio communications?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. Now, this is leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you rephrase the question, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure. Let me try. Although I think that in the questioning of Mr. Butler, that type of questioning was used extensively by Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, if you have objected to that questioning at that time, I take it that the Chamber has ruled on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In 10.3 -- actually, let me read from the English so that I can go faster. In the middle of the paragraph, you start and says: "That means that they could monitor, i.e., listen in on radio communications on HF and VHF maintained by RUP-4, RUP-15 and PRC-320 radio sets ..." What would they hear when listening in on radio transmissions across those devices that were encrypted by encryption devices?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I said that those pieces of equipment that were used most frequently - I mean, there were others as well - but an encoder could not be used on a VF; that is, 2 to 12 or 20 megahertz. So devices for encryption could not be attached to that. The only piece of equipment that provided a certain degree of protection was from the firm called Racal. They provided some protection. Others did not. Then if speeches encoded, then general encoding could be used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But the question, sir, was if a person listens to conversations going through these devices, what could that person hear? Can you tell us what the person could hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it is open, unsecured, then they will hear what is open. If it is encoded, they will hear that. Or if it's the Morris code, it will be A-B-C-D, but they will not be able to tell what the content is without decoding it. That's what I've already said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the same paragraph, you also talk of radio relay devices RRU-1, RDM-63, RRU-800 and FM200. When you say that the ABH could intercept these devices, what does that mean or presuppose?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the equipment that the VRS had could be listened in to by the ABiH except for communication through multiplex, or rather SMC. According to our information, they could not intercept that. The others, they could. Once they got in, they could listen in. But I already mentioned that encoding was used and they could not receive it as such. They can tape record it and then try to decode it somehow. And then what was transferred by KZ documents -- or rather general documents of the KZ, they could also tape record that and then try to decode it later. They didn't have any other way. They could listen into everything, relay, once they get into the beam. If they are not in the beam, of course they cannot intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say "in the beam," where is the beam or -- I think you -- I think you used the B/C/S term "snop," where is the "snop" located between radio relay devices?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said "snop," that is a term that is used in communications; that is to say, electromagnetic waves that are radiated by the transmitter station and that arrive at the receiver station, that is an electromagnetic wave, and I call that a "snop," "beam." Now, antennae, radio relay, they have a basic beam that goes directly from the antenna. However, in view of the imperfection of antennae, there are also those that go to the side. So these waves go laterally as well. So there is a bit that goes to the other side, but that is negligible. In order for someone to intercept, they have to get to the lateral wave in order to hear something.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say they have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we've dealt with the beams quite considerably. Now, if you think that this expert witness could add something to that? But what he told us until now is more or less in line with what those who were operating the systems told us. Then please focus on that. But it also -- I think there was not a major disagreement between the parties about what a beam means and what the effect is, that it limits intercepting from places outside that beam apart from how far the beam stretches, et cetera. But I didn't gain the impression, when listening to the other evidence, that there was a major dispute about that. About many other things there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Fair enough, Mr. President. Beams are straight and there is lateral parts, and those can be intercepted. That's -- we don't disagree with that. There is -- and sometimes it's hard to intercept. That's where we're at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It limits the possibilities of interception because it is in a specific direction and it's limited to the sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. It's limited to the -- to the "snop" and it's lateral affect, and if anyone can figure out what that is, great.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if that's the issue. And if you want to hear specific evidence on that, Mr. Ivetic, of course, that might add something, but then we would need focused questions specifically on that and then with all the details apart from the generalities we heard about already. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then I'd ask the witness in your answer you said: "In order for someone to intercept, they have to get to the lateral wave in order to hear something." You earlier identified the lateral as being negligible. Do you have any expression as to the type of distance that would be required; how close one would have to get to that antenna to catch its lateral dispersion of signal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Close to the antenna or close to the beam? What did you mean, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I meant the antenna because now we are talking about the antenna dispersing laterally, which is not the beam.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Best to hear that from the witness, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We just did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, you asked that. But I was just wondering whether -- okay. Could you explain to us how the lateral, if I could say dispersion, more or less, how that works and what -- how close you would have to be to the antenna to catch that, if I could say so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said that the lateral radiation, this fan, if you will, they are considerably weaker than the direct radiation of the beam. But they are much stronger than the posterior one. So better results are received if one can reach this lateral radiation. Now, how close the antenna has to be and how the receiver will receive this, it depends on the strength of the signal from the transmitting antenna and the sensitivity of the receiver. Now from the antenna, it gets weaker and weaker, and that is expressed in decibel. For each receiver, if one knows how far away the antenna is, a calculation can be made as to whether the signal could be received at all. Interceptors, of course, do not have that kind of information. And now they come in with their own antenna. When they see that there is a signal, then they receive that signal if it's strong enough. If it's not strong enough, they won't understand any of it. They can have it on an oscilloscope, for instance. But once they receive it on the receiver itself, it's not strong enough so that it could be useful for the radio reconnaissance people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just one last question about those lateral waves that I think should clarify everything. Geographically speaking, if we have two radio relay units communicating with each other, let's call them A and B, where would someone need to be situated geographically in order to catch that lateral dispersion of the signal?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lateral, in relation to the signal? The basic signal? Say maybe 80 degrees, left and right. Not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But the antenna to receive that lateral signal, where would it have to be placed in relation to the sender at A and the receiver at B?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to A and B, at least 80 degrees in order to get a usable and useful signal, because it is not 90 degrees. Say it's 80 degrees, left and right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I then try to find out whether I understood your last answer. If you say the signal is sent from A to B, that if you draw a line, and if you would then draw a line from this central connection between A and B to the left under an angle of 80 degrees of that line, and to the right also 80 degrees, that would then cover 160 degrees out of 360 degrees of the total circle. That within that area defined by those two lines, that there is a possibility of catching the signal that was intended to be sent from A to B?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we're at the time that you have indicated for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is time for the break. Witness, we'd like to see you back after half an hour. Mr. Ivetic, and I'll inquire as to where we are in times at this moment. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not you, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I understood that, Your Honours. We are at approximately -- let me see, I'm just getting rid of some questions that he has just answered. We have approximately 65 to 70 questions left, so we're looking at a little more than an hour remaining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Registrar, could you tell us how much of the -- I think two and a half hours, you indicated, that you would use --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Three and a half, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Three and a half. Well, we'll hear from you during the break. And if Mr. Ivetic would be interested, then -- Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: To the degree it may help, I think Mr. Ivetic will agree that our BiH and our MUP intercepts that we have from 1995, there is no evidence that any of those were unscrambled or decrypted, so to speak. That the evidence was they went out over the open air waves and were picked up. So we're not aware of any unscrambling done by the BiH and the MUP in terms of when they're hearing these intercepts. So just to try to clarify that. I think they may have broken a code or two along the way, but the actual unscrambling of a -- like a KZ encrypted line, no, we don't have any unscrambling, as you may recall from the evidence that came in years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I may correct counsel. There is a third party, who I shall not mention for fear of going beyond the Rule 70 requirements, but I believe the third party did identify breaking certain things that other parties did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's -- it's why I didn't mention that third -- that third party. I don't think -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you exclusively are talking about intercepts by the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the MUP --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the MUP, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- folks. So that -- so you can focus on that, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Further analysis of this may be rather complex, but inaccuracy of transcripts, possibly -- well, there are many ways of looking at it and each party will do it in its way, I take it. Mr. Ivetic, I'm informed that you used close to three hours by now. And I also noticed that here and then there is some overlap either with the report or with previous testimony. I hinted at that a few times. Could you please keep that in mind after we return and that will -- we'll resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Lukic, you wanted to raise a preliminary matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and in the absence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the absence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not important. I can use it, just half a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We just wanted to inform Your Honours that due to an inability to organise a videolink from Banja Luka, the next week we will have some empty space. We were not able to fill that gap with anybody else, so the next week we'll have only three witnesses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll have three witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the remainder of the examination for this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the witness can be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. But as long as we're briefly discussing scheduling issues, can I raise one matter that I think has a potentially significant impact on scheduling and that's simply this: The Court will recall that after making its oral rulings in relation to expert witnesses, it requested further submissions in relation to experts Poparic and Subotic and the motions to exclude. Those are completed. They are now pending. They have a potentially -- the resolution of that issue has a potentially significant issue on the estimated time for both sides, and I think I can speak for both sides in that respect, and the preparation time for the involved attorneys as well, a burden that could not easily be sustained, I think, at a late hour. So for both those reasons, we simply wanted to remind the Court that that it is pending and that the earlier it was resolved, the more positive impact it would have on both those factors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you would say we can use the time when we are not in Court to -- well, I'll not -- I'm kidding, a bit. But we'll certainly pay proper attention to resolve those matters as quickly as we can, because that's what both parties are interested in and the Chamber, of course, as well. The witness will be escorted into the courtroom. Further scheduling, Mr. Lukic. I think we will discuss it. As always, you are always encouraged to see whether you can, nevertheless, find solutions, but I do understand that there are serious problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 30 in the English and page 43 in the Serbian, I'd like to focus just briefly on footnote 39 of your report.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I found in some documents that the JNA and then the VRS communications were not secure because the company that produced the radio relay device AMD did not manufacture them properly, that communications via those devices were not secure, and some of these devices that were sold to the Gulf countries -- all the conversations on those devices were picked up, intercepted, and decoded by the USA very easily. So I can say that when the JNA decided to buy those devices, they considered all the options and decided to buy them but to change the -- some parts and some switches in the devices, so it was not possible to broadcast beyond what was set by the code and the key that much. I mean, there are many pages on the internet about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now if we can turn to page 36 in English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, whatever may have been about the internet, about selling, producing, et cetera, you said when the JNA bought these devices, it developed its own cryptographic data protection system device. Is that your personal knowledge? That's not what you learned from the internet, or was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is something that I learned from my colleague, a colonel who worked at the institute for applied mathematics, and that institute was the one that developed the code. So I didn't find out about it from the internet, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You heard that. When did it happen? When was the own cryptographic data protection system developed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I didn't ask that of my colleague, but I understood from the conversation that it was done at the time that device became part of the JNA arsenal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And when was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was sometime in 1975, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And it was still that same equipment that was used later with these adaptations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the change was made within the AMD device and the KZU-71. Changes were made in the device and certain switches were changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that a hardware change or was the data protection applied through software?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was made inside the AMD device, a part, a sector of the section of the device that is important for encryption was modified or changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But whether that was hardware or a software change, would you know that? If you don't know, tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a hardware change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that included also its own software?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the JNA software. The JNA had its own programmes for creating the key, then it had its own system for mixing the encoded parts of the tape and open parts of the -- the tape. It was TG-43. That was the -- and other parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one question to the witness. What is the name of your colleague, the colonel you referred to from whom you received this information? What was his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] His name is Zivko, Dzenopoljac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you perhaps repeat the family name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dzenopoljac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 36 in the English and page 54 in the Serbian of your report, I'd like to look at paragraph 11.11. In the fourth subparagraph of this introductory paragraph, it says that parabolic antenna are unsuitable for interception of frequencies under 1 gigahertz. Can you explain for us why that is.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see one of the parabolic antennas here. When you consider this, I believe for a number of reasons that it was not used for interception. And if you like, I can explain that later. Below 1 gigahertz, the reason is that these would be large antennas and then would need to be in balloons or some short of shelter. The antenna is then named after the shelter, "kaponir," and they are very visible. Regardless of the weather conditions and in order to reconnoiter properly, an antenna would need to be moved around.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You have analysed here in your report photo number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to call up P1649, which should be the source photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So ask you to identify items there -- in there so we can understand your report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, while we're waiting for that, Witness, could you tell us what would be the diameter needed for a parabolic antenna intercepting any signal under 1 gigahertz? What size, therefore?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Technical calculations are made for that. But in my estimate, I believe that the dish would need to be approximately 2 metres in diameter. Even 2 and a half metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, this is a photograph that is the source of your photo number 1, and you have identified certain antenna types by name. I'd like you to first, with the help of the usher, mark with a numeric number 1 and number 2 both of the Yagi antenna that you discuss in this photograph of your report.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Yagi antennas are the ones on the left pole. Number 1 indicates the first one, and number 2 indicates the second one. These are the Yagi antennas installed on the same antenna pole. One is installed horizontally, and the other vertically. The polarisation is changed with proximal antennas because then you could hear two signals that are close together, and you can do this also to augment a single signal. And their frequency goes up to 1.300 megahertz, which means that these antennae can be used for the interception of radio relay devices, RRU-1 and these others ones that are covered by the FMU and the RR-800 devices. This third antenna on the right close to the dish --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Before you talk about the next one, could you mark the one you are talking about with the number 3 and tell us what name of antenna it is so we can tie it to what you have written in your report?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is number 3. This is a logo-periodical antenna, or a "log-antenna" for short. It has a range from 40 to 800 megahertz, which means that it can monitor communications over the RRU-1 device. To the left of that antenna is the dish, parabolic antenna.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let the record reflect that has been marked as number 4. You've already told us about the parabolic antenna. You also mention an umbrella antenna. Could you mark the umbrella antenna with a number 5.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There it is, number 5 in the corner. You can't see all of it. All you can see are the lateral spikes. It's known as an umbrella antenna in jargon, because it reminds you of an umbrella. It's an antenna from the set of devices that I mentioned, the ICR-100 for example. For the reception of frequencies of 180 megahertz. It has circular radiation and reception, so it's not necessary to point it or direct it towards the source, because it receives all around and transmits also in a complete circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just waiting for the translation. Can we now tender the photo as marked, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit D1194. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, all five antennas.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in your report at page 32 in English and in Serbian it's page 46, you have also document number 3, which should not be broadcast. I'd like to call up the source of that, which is 1D05807 which, likewise, should not be broadcast. And without identifying the names of the southern and northern locations, can you tell us what is depicted herein?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This topographical map refers to both of the locations, the northern and the southern location. And this is definitely a map that was part of the documents that were received by the commander of the southern facility. And you can see that certain zones were set there; zone number 1, number 2, going from the left to the right - 1, 2, 3, and 4. And then earlier reconnaissance established some earlier locations of some listening stations, and they are mentioned here. Since I said that the B and H Army did not have any locators or radio search devices, they probably directed their antennas, and whenever they received the best signal on their receivers, they would understand from that that the listening-in device was in that route. They probably -- the officers knew what their forward forces were and those of the enemy, the forces of Republika Srpska. And knowing the manner in which these devices worked, they would estimate the elevation at which the device would need to be directed. So this was -- you could see that it wasn't done very precisely. On the example of the Veliki Zep node, 1 centimetre on the map is 1 kilometre actually in the field. So when you look at it here, you could see that the stations are at least 2 kilometres away from each other, but that's not true because all of them were actually clustered at Veliki Zep. Also indicating that they didn't have the most precise data is the fact that they worked amongst themselves, that two of them worked together. And that's not very logical. If one radio relay is working, it would be facing a specific unit or a feature. They should not just be oscillating in the area between them. So they would need to be linked to some facility that would be intercepting all the communications from all the brigades. They did know that these were brigades, however, because they had some intercepted material, most probably. And, secondly, TO brigades were formed in the territory of the former B and H -- yes, yes. I apologise. And the TO had its own brigades, which were called according to the settlements or places where they were formed, so on the basis of that, they could determine that that would be such-and-such a brigade using such-and-such a device.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can I object for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't think you can object to an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know what the objection is about. Is it about a question, is it about a --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can we have some foundation on whose map this is? We're going into a lot of detail about it with no foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, as a matter of fact, I would have left you with all the questions about this map. But if they would not have included who produced it, then I would have asked for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we can call up 1D5798, but that should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we have an answer to the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When we move this map away, unless you want to have it back later and then put --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the question to the witness, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I want to go with a document that depicts what's on the map that shows who would have created it. That's what I want to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Which I think was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will learn that from that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's wait and see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, in the map we had zones 1, 2, 3, and 4 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can -- I apologise. This is a document dated the 21st of August, 1995 from the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And we have zones 1, 2, 3, and 4 depicted in the centre. Could you please, for our purposes, sir, read the B/C/S there and tell us how it corresponds to the zones that we had on the map. And perhaps it might assist if we have on one half of the screen the map and on one half of the screen the document. That might help us follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Same objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps we first ask the witness or you give further information as where the document comes from, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This document comes from EDS given to us by the Office of the Prosecutor, Mr. McCloskey, sitting across this room.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I was hoping he would ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there are a few matters. Witness, this document that you see on the screen at this moment, that's the written document to the left, are you familiar with that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, Your Honour, are you addressing me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am familiar with this document. I received it -- actually, first I received the map. And then after that was printed, or after my material was printed, then I received this too. On the basis of the map itself, one could conclude that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. We are not there yet. When did you -- and I'm exclusively talking about the written text, not the map. When did you see that for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I first saw it in May, June. That's when I received it. This year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of this year. From whom did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The lawyers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do I understand that you said that you received after that the map? Oh, no. You first received the map as far as I'm -- I'm apologising because I think I misrepresented what you said. So you first received the map also from the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then later you received that document. Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- do you have any personal knowledge about the document so as to where it came from, when it was drafted? Do you know anything about that? Or, if not, please tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I have no idea whatsoever. I know what is written here. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear. Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe I had already asked a question to have you read what zones 1, 2, 3, and 4 are depicted on the document and to comment upon the map, how those correlate to what is depicted on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is there an English translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There is not. That's why I want the witness to read it so that we get the English, otherwise I would -- otherwise it would be self-evident.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It meant it -- to read the part that says "zones 1, 2, 3, and 4." We don't need to read the heading which might mention --

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. I understand. Zone 1 that was received by the commander of this facility. To the left is Vozuca; in depth, Banja Luka; to the right, Doboj; azimuth, 293 to 320.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please read slower.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you read slower because the interpreters are unable to follow you. So could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- slowly repeat what you read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zone 1: To the left, Vozuca; in depth, Banja Luka; to the right, Doboj; azimuth, from 295 to 320. Zone 2: To the left, Zvornik; in depth, Sarajevo, the Drina river; to the right, Nisici; azimuth, from 80 to 190. Zone 3: To the left, Brcko; in depth, the Sava and the Drina; to the right, Zvornik; azimuth from 20 to 80 degrees. Zone 4: To the left, Doboj; in depth, the Sava; to the right, Brcko; azimuth, from 320 to 20 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, now could you comment, based upon your viewing this map that is on the right-hand side, how the zones referenced in the document correlate to the zones on the map?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These zones that are written down in this document and the zones that are marked on this work map, they correspond to one another. And from this, one can see that the task was for this facility to intercept communications of the Drina Corps, the Eastern Bosnian Corps, and the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if I can direct your attention to the second paragraph before it says "zone 1," that starts "dalje sada ima." And if I can ask you to read that paragraph for us.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Further on, there is this rubric, location of participant. Please, who, amongst us, can write that, where the participants are? Unless the Chetniks listen to the order themselves and tell us themselves where they are. We still have the valid distribution of the so-called zones of RE. We can write them and comment upon them." And then the rest follows down here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You earlier mentioned a document from 1995 that led you to believe that the ABiH did not know where our nodes were located. When I say "our," I mean "VRS nodes" are located. Can you tell us if this is that document you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the strongest evidence. Although even through previous documents, I saw that they did not really have information on the locations involved in terms of these radio relay locations activated in the Drina Corps. And I did not receive any information as to what they knew about the other corps that they were following.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could, Your Honours, mark for identification 1D5798, pending a full translation of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you done with the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we do so. Witness, you read a certain line to us. "Further on, there is this rubric. Location of participant," it says. You are, in your answer, suggesting that the location is the location of any communication centre. Where does that appear clearly, if it does, in this line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it says: "Please, which one of us can say who, where" -- or rather, "... where some of the participants are." And when he says "participants," he means a radio relay station that he is intercepting, listening to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it's on the basis of the word "participants" that you conclude that this is how it has to be understood.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, the document, that's not the map yet, Mr. Ivetic, just the document, would receive what number, when it's marked for identification, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit D1195. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification. Are you going to return to the map, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I leave it in your hands, Your Honour. A smaller version of the map is already included in the report of the expert at page 46 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'd object to him -- telling him what's in his own report after he was asked where the document came from and didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I allowed to answer the Judge's question? Your Honour asked me what I want to do with the report that relates to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I may have -- I may have misunderstood it in the sense that whether you wanted to ask further questions about the map and that -- in that way, to return to the map itself. I do understand that you leave it in our hands whether you want to have it separately --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- exhibited or as it appears in the report. Now, Witness, you said you received this map first. Do you know anything about where it comes from, who drafted it, when it was drafted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is no date on it, there is no signature, and I can just conclude that this task was probably given by the commander of the unit who was the commander of both of these facilities and that this pertains to this southern point, here. Now, the map was made at sometime, say, in 1993, 1994, when they already had some information about some deployment of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, are you speculating or do you have any knowledge which makes you believe that it may have been made in 1993 or 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my assumption, Your Honour. I have no data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Ivetic, you apparently provided the witness with the map. Is it a map that was disclosed to you by the Prosecution? Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. McCloskey, do you have any information as to where the map comes from?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if you consider it not a good idea to tell it in the presence of the witness, then we would hear that at another point in time later. But I would have another question for you, Witness. Have you analysed the content of this map, and have you asked yourself what it depicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I've already said that this is one of the documents, orders that are being sent to the commander of this facility to the south. It's part of an order, and we assume that it's his superior officer that is issuing this. I did not see any other documents in addition to this map, and I am not aware of any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say it's part of an order. How do you know that it's part of an order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would only be natural. When an order is being issued, it would be quite natural, normal, along with an order to reconnoiter that one provides a map for the reconnaissance involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you assume that it's a conclusion rather than any specific knowledge. Have you looked at the accuracy of what is depicted on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've already mentioned that that is partial knowledge about the location and number of radio relay stations used by the VRS. The locations are not fully correct. And also the number, as we can see from those documents, the number of radio relay devices used. There is another symptomatic thing. Not a single radio relay RRU-1 was identified. Or maybe this person did not believe that it was important, that that information should be contained in this map, but I believe that he didn't have the information in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I take you to zone 4 on the map. The azimuth angle there is described as 80 degrees. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I do see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you think it's 80 degrees, that angle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a protractor. Maybe it's not all of 80, but it's around that figure. 90 would be a full one, and this is somewhat less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know why it says 80 degrees or -- and can you read what is in zone 1? Can you decipher what is ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zone 1 says 25 degrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just 25. And then over there, there is 80. So that would -- well, 80, that's quite big.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any comment, then, on the accuracy of those two figures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My comment would be that it wasn't done very professionally and with the aides that one should use when working on a map. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey, would you give any further information at this point in time, where we're about to decide on admission, yes or no? Witness, you understand the English language, don't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very, very small.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You greeted me this morning in English, I think, when you entered the courtroom. And I think it would be safer not to just ask the witness to take off his earphones but to ask him to leave, if it's to be done at this very moment, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this witness has relied on a former expert for a lot of his report, an expert called Rodic, which I'm sure Mr. Ivetic knows about, from, I believe, the Popovic case. This map is part of Rodic's report, which was attached as an annex to this man's report. Whether Rodic made this map or he got it from somewhere else, I'm not -- my Popovic memory is not all it could be. We're looking into that. But this does not have -- I don't have any recollection of the 2nd Corps or the MUP making such a map. But ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- a complicated issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Prosecution has its doubts on the provenance of this document to say where it comes from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, it comes from Rodic's report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. But whether it was originally drafted for that report or whether it came from another source is still --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's still an open question. I believe it's a -- I think he's -- I think it was done by Rodic, but before I can tell you that, I need to get back into our history a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the other document -- well, first of all, the Chamber will decide on admission of this map at the end of the examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do I need to tender it then, Your Honours? Because I have not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You have not tendered it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you do not intend to tender it either.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I had left it up to Your Honours whether you thought we needed the bigger portion of it because there is a smaller portion in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you would say the -- perhaps if only for purposes of knowing that this map and admission of this map needs, perhaps, specific attention that we put it as a separate --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if you would tender it at this moment as a separate document, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it would be marked for identification. Mr. Registrar, the map as a separate document would receive number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Under seal, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under seal. Under seal. D1195, which was the document, the text document, should have been admitted under -- should have been marked for identification under seal then, as well, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And are there similar questions as to the provenance of that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, that -- it looks like a BiH document, and I don't right now have reason to have any problems with it. I think it's got an ERN on it. We best take a look, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But for the time being, therefore, we leave it to you whether you want to make any further submissions in relation to that. Then we can move on, I think, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although I think you went well over your time, but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's all very important and I'm trying to respond to questions raised by Your Honours several times today to try to make the technical matters understood for all of us. If we could now move to 1D1082, and this also should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We had earlier looked at a photograph of antenna from the so-called northern facility. This is dated in, I think, February of 1995 from the northern facility and is an overview of posts and equipment. Now, looking at the antenna listed for these three posts that we have here - 1, 2, and 3 - have we seen them all in the one picture that we have looked at thus far?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't -- I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we look at the document, we have listed three work positions or posts, and we have three devices, an ICR-100 two times and an ICR-7100. And in the column "Antenna" we have listed Helical AH-7000 and log periodic. Which of these antennae have we already seen in the one photograph that we have looked at?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have these AH-7000 antennas, that's the umbrella antenna. I described it as that. Then we have the regular logo ones. And then we have the Helical antennas. But they're not here in the picture. We've got the parabolic ones, not the Helical.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, first of all, post 1 has an ICR-100 receiver and a TS-430S transceiver and a converter 150/18 megahertz. What does that tell you about the probable use of this post, including if it is suitable for listening to VRS radio relay transmissions?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was a Helical antenna here, then you could intercept multichannel communications. That kind of antenna does have the range for the RRU-800, the TS-430S splitter can split channels 1 to 12 or 1 to 8 if a different device is involved. And then the Helical antenna can receive all of that. This converter then is not needed in that case for this particular post. Perhaps if there was a different device of a high frequency when you are switching from a higher to a lower frequency in order to split it, then you would have some special post. But in this case, there isn't one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, post number 2 has an ICR-7100 device attached to the AH-7000 which you've identified as the parabolic antenna. Based on your knowledge, experience and expertise, what use do you foresee of this post? Can it effectively intercept VRS radio relay transmissions at the -- at the northern location?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood it as post number 2. Post number 2 has a discount antenna, so it cannot receive multi-channel signals from an RRU-800 or an FM200.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I misspoke. Thank you for correcting me. And I think you've already identified the use of the log-periodic antenna in one of your previous answers, so I'd like to then try to save time by first tendering this document under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could I ask a very short question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document refers to tape recorders as UHER4000, U-H-E-R. In your report, you are referring to UHR, that is U-H-R tape recorders. Is that the same? I take it it is, UHER being a well-known company producing professional recording devices? It's in paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in my document there is a photograph of an UHER tape recorder where we have written the letters UHER4000 report, IC. If anything else is written, then it must mean that it's a typo. But it's that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then a number, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be assigned Exhibit D1197. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could look at P164 -- under seal, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could look at P1648. And this will be the original source of picture number 2 from page 54 and page 36 of your report in the respective Serbian and English languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And this is also represented as being the northern site. Now, you have mentioned a couple of times a heliocodial [sic] antenna. In this photograph, can you, with the assistance of the usher, circle the heliocodial antenna.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Given the proximity of the two different types of antennas, I would ask that you actually circle the heliocodial in addition to marking it number 1.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number 1 marks this antenna that is like a pipe, that is the heliocodial antenna which listens into the RRU-800 or the FM200.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it is not the red and white striped longer antenna but the shorter one immediately left to the number 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now this longer red and white antenna, which I believe is a logo-periodic, in this configuration does it work in conjunction with the heliocodial antenna or not? That is to say, does it add anything to what the heliocodial antenna can do on its own?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not contribute to the operation of this antenna because they are on different wavelengths. The heliocodial antenna receives the frequency of range. It's not precise but it's approximately from 500 to 1.200 megahertz, and within that range the RRU-800 and FM200 go up to 960 megahertz; whereas, the log antenna receives frequencies up to 1300 megahertz. So they don't cancel each other out.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And does the logo antenna in this picture -- what's your opinion as to whether it is a professionally manufactured antenna or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the photograph, you can tell that it's a handmade antenna, constructed from materials and parts from other antennas. And it can serve its purpose, definitely. It's not of any high quality, but still it can serve the purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could tender the document under seal as marked or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it needs to be under seal or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it not a P number?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is a P number, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's been marked though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now it's marked. Mr. Registrar, the document now marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It shall be assigned Exhibit D1198. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1198 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to now look at D310 which is represented as being from the southern location and again has a number of antenna or antennae.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the one in the centre that has a pipe and a spiralling wire or spiralling-something across it, what kind of an antenna is that?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also a heliocodial antenna intended for the reception of RRU-800 and FM200. And it's a hand-manufactured antenna. One first calculates the thickness of the pipe, the thickness of the wire that is wrapped around the pipe, the distance between them, so that it is capable of receiving a certain signal. When these calculations are made, usually they are done for one frequency. But probably the person who constructed it thought that they probably needed 800 megahertz in order to be able to receive from 600 to 800, and then from 800 up to 960. The quality is not as good as factory-manufactured antennas. The problem is the cable that is seen here in the shape of a semicircle. They have to be made from material which would ensure that there is good connections as well as the possibility of adjusting the antenna, so I don't know with this kind of home-manufactured antenna how much you could receive on it. But definitely, it was substandard in quality in comparison to factory-manufactured antennas.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can any of the other antennas we see in this photograph be used in conjunction with the heliocodial homemade antenna to assist in its reception of signal?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, heliocodial antennas, mostly you cannot increase the signal. Perhaps at some lower frequencies. But in this particular one, you cannot match. The only thing that is possible is to have two antennas working in tandem.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can look at, first of all, briefly just D309. This is also reported to be from the southern condition -- southern position. I'd like to direct your attention first to the post on the right-hand side that appears to have a piece of metal with a hole in it that is detached from it. Could you tell us what the significance is of that post and that piece of metal that has a hole that is detached from the main post?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you can see on the right-hand side is a metal pipe. It probably carried an antenna at some point. You can see at the top that there was some kind of item on the top, and it's 99.9 per cent sure that it was grounding that was there that has become disconnected. I think it wasn't done very well because the grounding would take care of the safety of the personnel but would also maintain the signal in case of electric discharges or lightening striking the pole.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last sentence of your answer so that the translators can accurately translate it.

utterances.speaker: MILE DOSENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. When you look at this whole thing, you can see that the personnel was not very conscientious because they didn't ensure proper grounding which would safeguard the personnel as well as the actual device from lightening or electrical discharge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm looking at the clock. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah. I guess we'll stop for today. I have approximately, I'd say, 15 minutes more to cover three brief areas; one document from the southern location, and two diagrams showing the optical visibility from ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you'll be given such extra time, because I know that you blamed the Chamber more or less for the time you took. Perhaps evidence elicited should be so clear as not for the Chamber to ask for further explanations. And apart from that, you -- we noticed two things: First, that you let the witness go often far beyond what your question is without efficiently stopping him and getting him back on track. The second thing is that you often dealt with such technical details that questions may be put as to the relevance and the probative value of such questioning. So, therefore, we'll consider - and you should prepare for even a little bit less time - and focus on the most important matters. Mr. Dosenovic, we would like to see you back. But we are not sitting tomorrow, which means that we would like to see you back Monday morning, 9.30 in the morning, and -- Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Just one thing that may be helpful. Those photographs or OTP photographs that were taken in 1998, just so you could have the context while we're still thinking about them, is from the sites, as Mr. Ivetic mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's comment. I think -- that's comment not necessarily to be done in the presence of the witness. I also do not fully grasp, but I'm not inviting you at this moment to further elaborate, Mr. McCloskey, what the message exactly is you're sending to us, because I was at this moment telling the witness that we expected him back at 9.30 in the morning on Monday. And I again instruct you that you should not speak or communicate, not by any technical means, with anyone about your testimony, whether that is testimony you have given already or testimony still to be given on Monday, and hopefully not on Tuesday. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn and will resume Monday, the 17th of August, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 17th day of August, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.17 p.m.,
